findings.title: Failed type creation can be committed as a successful placement run
findings.body: After duplicating the base type, either parameter assignment or validation can return false without deleting the new type or rolling back that unit of work. If the orchestrator handles the false result by skipping the foundation and returns normally, Execute unconditionally commits the transaction and reports foundationsData.Count as created, leaving an invalid or partially configured duplicate type and silently missing a foundation. Make type creation atomic (for example with a SubTransaction that is rolled back on every failure), propagate placement failures to Execute, and report the actual number of instances created.

findings.title: Transitive endpoint grouping can discard valid foundations
findings.body: Lines are grouped transitively whenever adjacent members share an endpoint within 0.01, but the entire connected component is later ignored when its overall Z range exceeds 0.01. For example, otherwise valid closed outlines at elevations 0, 0.009, and 0.018 that touch at CAD endpoints become one component through transitive matches; its range is 0.018, so all outlines are silently discarded. Connectivity must not merge components beyond the elevation tolerance, or each component must be partitioned by a stable elevation criterion before polygon extraction.
